questions.stem: A solenoid of $1200$ turns is wound uniformly in a single layer on a glass tube $2$ m long and $0.2$ m in diameter. The magnetic intensity at the center of the solenoid when a current of $2$ A flows through it is:
questions.solution:
Number of turns $N = 1200$, length $2$ m, so $n = \dfrac{1200}{2}$ per metre; current $I = 2$ A.

Magnetic field inside the solenoid: $B = \mu_0 n I$

Magnetic intensity: $H = \dfrac{B}{\mu_0} = nI = \left(\dfrac{1200}{2}\right)(2) = 1.2 \times 10^{3}\ \text{A m}^{-1}$ $\quad (\because B = \mu_0 H)$

questions.stem: In the given circuit, rms value of current ($I_{rms}$) through the resistor $R$ is:
The variation of kinetic energy (KE) of a particle executing simple harmonic motion with the displacement ($x$) starting from mean position to extreme position ($A$) is given by
questions.solution:
$$T.E = K.E + P.E \Rightarrow K.E = T.E - P.E = \frac{1}{2}kA^2 - \frac{1}{2}kx^2$$

$$\Rightarrow KE = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2) \quad [\because k = m\omega^2]$$

KE is maximum at $x = 0$ and zero when $x = A$. $\therefore$ K.E. vs $x$ graph is a parabola.

questions.stem: A projectile is projected at $30^\circ$ from horizontal with initial velocity $40\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The velocity of the projectile at $t = 2$ s from the start will be: (Given $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$u = 40$ m/s, $\theta = 30^\circ$

Time of flight $T = \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g} = \dfrac{2 \times 40 \times 1}{10 \times 2} = 4$ s

So at $t = 2$ s the projectile is at maximum height, where the vertical component of velocity is zero.

$$v = u\cos\theta = 40\cos 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$

questions.stem: On a temperature scale 'X', the boiling point of water is $65^\circ X$ and the freezing point is $-15^\circ X$. Assume that the X scale is linear. The equivalent temperature corresponding to $-95^\circ X$ on the Fahrenheit scale would be:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{X - LFP}{UFP - LFP} = \frac{T_F - 32}{212 - 32}$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{-95 - (-15)}{65 - (-15)} = \frac{T_F - 32}{180} \Rightarrow \frac{-80}{80} = \frac{T_F - 32}{180}$$

$$\Rightarrow T_F = -180 + 32 = -148^\circ F$$

questions.stem: The logic operations performed by the given digital circuit is equivalent to:
questions.solution:
Output of the first NAND gate: $X_1 = \overline{A \cdot B}$; output of the other NAND gate: $X_2 = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

The next NAND gate gives $X_3 = \overline{X_1 \cdot X_2} = \overline{\overline{A\cdot B} \cdot \overline{A \cdot B}} = A \cdot B$.

The NOT gate then gives $Y = \overline{X_3}$; as printed, the final output simplifies to $Y = A \cdot B$, i.e. the circuit is equivalent to an AND gate.

questions.stem: A bowl filled with very hot soup cools from $98^\circ C$ to $86^\circ C$ in $2$ minutes when the room temperature is $22^\circ$C. How long it will take to cool from $75^\circ C$ to $69^\circ C$?
questions.solution:
Newton's law of cooling (average form): $\dfrac{\Delta T}{\Delta t} = k(T_{avg} - T_0)$

First phase ($98 \to 86^\circ$C): $\Delta t = 2$ min, $T_{avg} = \dfrac{98+86}{2} = 92^\circ$C

$$\frac{12}{2} = k(92 - 22) \Rightarrow k = \frac{6}{70}$$

Second phase ($75 \to 69^\circ$C): $T_{avg} = \dfrac{75+69}{2} = 72^\circ$C

$$\Delta t = \frac{6}{k(72-22)} = \frac{6 \times 70}{6 \times 50} = 1.4\ \text{minutes}$$

questions.stem: Two identical particles each of mass $m$ go round a circle of radius $a$ under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The angular speed of each particle will be:
questions.solution:
The particles are diametrically opposite, so their separation is $2a$.

$$F = \frac{Gm^2}{(2a)^2} = \frac{Gm^2}{4a^2}$$

This provides the centripetal force $m\omega^2 a$:

$$\frac{Gm^2}{4a^2} = m\omega^2 a \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\frac{Gm}{4a^3}}$$

questions.stem: Two resistances are given as $R_1 = (10 \pm 0.5)\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = (15 \pm 0.5)\ \Omega$. The percentage error in the measurement of equivalent resistance when they are connected in parallel is:
questions.solution:
Parallel: $\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{6} \Rightarrow R_{eq} = 6\ \Omega$

For error:
$$\frac{dR_{eq}}{R_{eq}^2} = \frac{dR_1}{R_1^2} + \frac{dR_2}{R_2^2} \Rightarrow dR_{eq} = 36\left(\frac{0.5}{100} + \frac{0.5}{225}\right) = 36 \times 0.5 \times \frac{13}{900} = \frac{26}{100}$$

$$\%\ \text{error} = \frac{dR_{eq}}{R_{eq}} \times 100 = \frac{26/100}{6} \times 100 = \frac{26}{6} = 4.33$$

questions.stem: A hypothetical gas expands adiabatically such that its volume changes from $08$ litres to $27$ litres. If the ratio of final pressure of the gas to initial pressure of the gas is $\dfrac{16}{81}$. Then the ratio of $\dfrac{C_p}{C_V}$ will be
questions.solution:
$V_i = 8$ litre, $V_f = 27$ litre, $\dfrac{p_f}{p_i} = \dfrac{16}{81}$

For an adiabatic process $pV^\gamma = $ constant:

$$\frac{p_f}{p_i} = \left(\frac{V_i}{V_f}\right)^\gamma \Rightarrow \frac{16}{81} = \left(\frac{8}{27}\right)^\gamma \Rightarrow \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4 = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3\gamma}$$

$$3\gamma = 4 \Rightarrow \gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_V} = \frac{4}{3}$$
questions.notes: pressure ratio printed as 1/8 in stem (cut off); solution uses 16/81, which is consistent with answer

questions.stem: The torque of a force $5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$ about the origin is $\tau$. If the force acts on a particle whose position vector is $2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, then the value of $\tau$ will be:
questions.solution: $$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 & -7 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-14-3) - \hat{j}(-14-5) + \hat{k}(6-10) = -17\hat{i} + 19\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$$

questions.stem: If $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{K}$ represent electric field and propagation vectors of the EM waves in vacuum, then magnetic field vector is given by: ($\omega$ angular frequency)
questions.solution:
Magnetic field vector is in the direction of $\hat{K} \times \hat{E}$, with magnitude $B = \dfrac{E}{c} = \dfrac{K}{\omega}E$.

$$\therefore \vec{B} = \frac{1}{\omega}(\vec{K} \times \vec{E})$$
questions.subtopic: Relation between E, B and k

questions.stem: A thin prism $P_1$ with an angle $6^\circ$ and made of glass of refractive index $1.54$ is combined with another prism $P_2$ made from glass of refractive index $1.72$ to produce dispersion without average deviation. The angle of prism $P_2$ is:
questions.solution:
For no average deviation, $\delta_1 = \delta_2$:

$$6^\circ(1.54 - 1) = A(1.72 - 1) \Rightarrow A = \frac{6^\circ \times 0.54}{0.72} = \frac{18^\circ}{4} = 4.5^\circ$$

questions.stem: A flask contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of $2 : 1$ by mass at temperature $27^\circ$C. The ratio of average kinetic energy per molecule of hydrogen and oxygen respectively is:
questions.solution:
$K_{av} = \dfrac{5}{2}kT$ for both diatomic gases at the same temperature.

Ratio $= 1 : 1$

questions.stem: The magnetic moments associated with two closely wound circular coils $A$ and $B$ of radius $r_A = 10$ cm and $r_B = 20$ cm respectively are equal if: (Where $N_A, I_A$ and $N_B, I_B$ are number of turns and current of $A$ and $B$ respectively)
questions.solution:
$M = NIA$, $M_A = M_B$

$$N_AI_A\pi(0.1)^2 = N_BI_B\pi(0.2)^2 \Rightarrow N_AI_A = 4N_BI_B$$

questions.stem: Two radioactive elements A and B initially have same number of atoms. The half life of $A$ is same as the average life of $B$. If $\lambda_A$ and $\lambda_B$ are decay constants of A and B respectively, then choose the correct relation from the given options.
questions.solution: $$T_{1/2}(A) = T_{av}(B) \Rightarrow \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda_A} = \frac{1}{\lambda_B} \Rightarrow \lambda_A = \lambda_B \ln 2$$

questions.stem: The angular momentum for the electron in Bohr's orbit is $L$. If the electron is assumed to revolve in second orbit of hydrogen atom, then the change in angular momentum will be:
questions.solution:
$L_n = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$. In the first orbit $L = \dfrac{h}{2\pi}$; in the second orbit $L_2 = \dfrac{2h}{2\pi} = 2L$.

Change in angular momentum $= 2L - L = L$.
questions.notes: solution completed by transcriber; printed options were garbled (L/2, L, L, K) and restored to the original JM 2023 options; printed solution belonged to another question

questions.stem: Ratio of thermal energy released in two resistor $R$ and $3R$ connected in parallel in an electric circuit is:
questions.solution:
$H = \dfrac{V^2}{R} \times t$ (same $V$ in parallel)

$$\frac{H_1}{H_2} = \frac{V^2t/R}{V^2t/3R} = 3 : 1$$

questions.stem: In a cuboid of dimension $2L \times 2L \times L$, a charge $q$ is placed at the centre of the surface 'S' having area of $4L^2$. The flux through the opposite surface to 'S' is given by
questions.solution:
Place an identical cuboid on the other side of S to form a cube of side $2L$ with $q$ at its centre, as shown in the figure. Each face of the cube gets $\phi = \dfrac{q/\varepsilon_0}{6}$.

Flux passing through the shaded face $= \dfrac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$

questions.stem: Two bodies are having kinetic energies in the ratio $16 : 9$. If they have same linear momentum, the ratio of their masses respectively is:
questions.solution: $$\frac{K_1}{K_2} = \frac{p_1^2}{2m_1} \times \frac{2m_2}{p_2^2} = \frac{m_2}{m_1} = \frac{16}{9} \Rightarrow \frac{m_1}{m_2} = \frac{9}{16}$$

questions.stem: The frequency ($v$) of an oscillating liquid drop may depend upon radius ($r$) of the drop, density ($\rho$) of liquid and the surface tension ($s$) of the liquid as: $v = r^a\rho^b s^c$. The values of $a$, $b$ and $c$ respectively are
questions.solution:
$$[T^{-1}] = [L]^a[ML^{-3}]^b\left[\frac{MLT^{-2}}{L}\right]^c \Rightarrow T^{-1} = M^{b+c}L^{a-3b}T^{-2c}$$

$c = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $b = -\dfrac{1}{2}$, $a - 3b = 0 \Rightarrow a + \dfrac{3}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow a = -\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.stem:
Young's moduli of the material of wires A and B are in the ratio of $1 : 4$, while its area of cross sections are in the ratio of $1 : 3$. If the same amount of load is applied to both the wires, the amount of elongation produced in the wires A and B will be in the ratio of
[Assume length of wires A and B are same]
questions.solution:
$\Delta L = \dfrac{FL}{AY}$

$$\frac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B} = \frac{A_B}{A_A}\cdot\frac{Y_B}{Y_A} = 3 \times 4 = 12$$

questions.stem: A single slit of width $a$ is illuminated by a monochromatic light of wavelength $600$ nm. The value of '$a$' for which first minimum appears at $\theta = 30^\circ$ on the screen will be:
questions.solution:
Condition for first minimum: $a\sin\theta = \lambda$

$$a\sin 30^\circ = 600 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{m} \Rightarrow a = 1200 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{m} = 1.2\ \mu\text{m}$$

questions.stem: A $12$ V battery connected to a coil of resistance $6\ \Omega$ through a switch, drives a constant current in the circuit. The switch is opened in $1$ ms. The emf induced across the coil is $20$ V. The inductance of the coil is:
questions.solution:
$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2$ A initially, and $I = 0$ after the switch is opened.

$$\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = \frac{-2}{1 \times 10^{-3}} = -2 \times 10^{3}\ \text{A/s}$$

$$e = -L\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \Rightarrow 20 = -L \times (-2 \times 10^{3}) \Rightarrow L = 0.01\ \text{H} = 10\ \text{mH}$$

questions.stem: A passenger sitting in a train A moving at $90$ km/h observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for $8$ s. If the velocity of the train B is $54$ km/h, then length of train B is:
questions.solution:
$V_A = 90 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 25$ m/s, $V_B = 54 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 15$ m/s

Velocity of train B w.r.t. train A $= \vec{V}_B - \vec{V}_A = 15 - (-25) = 40$ m/s

$$\text{Time of crossing} = \frac{\text{length of train}}{\text{relative velocity}} \Rightarrow 8 = \frac{\ell}{40} \Rightarrow \ell = 320\ \text{m}$$

questions.stem: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle are accelerated from rest by $2$ V and $4$ V potentials, respectively. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelength is:
questions.solution:
$$\lambda = \frac{h}{mv} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mq\Delta V}}$$

$$\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p} = \sqrt{\frac{m_pV_pq_p}{m_\alpha V_\alpha q_\alpha}} = \sqrt{\frac{1 \times 2 \times 1}{4 \times 4 \times 2}} = \frac{1}{4}$$

$$\Rightarrow \lambda_p : \lambda_\alpha = 4 : 1$$
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
questions.notes: potential of proton cut off in image; 2 V inferred from printed solution

questions.stem: The engine of a train moving with speed $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards a platform sounds a whistle at frequency $400$ Hz. The frequency heard by a passenger inside the train is (neglect air speed. Speed of sound in air $330\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: The relative velocity of the passenger with respect to the source of sound (engine) is zero, so there is no Doppler effect. Frequency heard is $400$ Hz.

questions.stem: If $V$ is the gravitational potential due to sphere of uniform density on its surface, then its value at the center of sphere will be:
A capacitor of capacitance $C$ is charged to a potential $V$. The flux of the electric field through a closed surface enclosing the positive plate of the capacitor is:
questions.solution: $$\phi = \frac{q_{in}}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{CV}{\varepsilon_0}$$

questions.stem: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady speed of $10$ cm/s. If the drops coalesce, the new velocity is:-
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity $v \propto r^2$, so $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)^2$

$$8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \Rightarrow R = 2r$$

$$\frac{10}{v_2} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \Rightarrow v_2 = 40\ \text{cm/s}$$

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement.

options.text: Gangue is an ore contaminated with undesired materials.
The scientific and technological process used for isolation of the metal from its ore is known as metallurgy.
Minerals are naturally occurring chemical substances in the earth's crust.
Ores are minerals that may contain a metal.

questions.solution: Gangue is the commercially worthless material which contaminates the ore (it is not the ore itself).

questions.stem: A $0.5$ molal solution of ethylene glycol in water is used as coolant in a car. If the freezing point constant of water be $1.86^\circ$C per mole, the mixture shall freeze at
questions.solution:
$\Delta T_f = K_f \times m = 1.86 \times 0.5 = 0.93^\circ$C

$T_f = -0.93^\circ$C

questions.stem:
The reaction

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CO} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$
questions.solution: This is the Gattermann–Koch reaction; it proceeds in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ or CuCl.

questions.stem: Which will not result in the formation of anisole?
questions.solution: In the last case, the acidic phenol proton destroys the Grignard reagent and $\text{CH}_4$ is produced, not anisole.

questions.stem: The starting material for the manufacture of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is
questions.solution: Pyrolusite (it is $\text{MnO}_2$).

questions.stem: Which of the following oxo acid of sulphur has O-O bond?
questions.solution: Peroxodisulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$), $\text{HO–SO}_2\text{–O–O–SO}_2\text{–OH}$, contains an O–O bond, as shown in the figure.

questions.stem:
Identify correct reactivity order for $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction

(i), (ii), (iii) as shown in the figure.
questions.solution:
Carbocations formed (as shown in the figure): from (i) aromatic, but O exerts maximum $-I$ effect; from (ii) aromatic, N exerts less $-I$; from (iii) anti-aromatic (least stable).

Hence reactivity: (ii) > (i) > (iii).

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to prevent the decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$?
questions.solution: Urea acts as a stabilising agent. It prevents the decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

questions.stem: Primary amines can be distinguished from secondary and tertiary amines by reacting with
questions.solution: $1^\circ$ amines (aliphatic and aromatic) react with $\text{CHCl}_3/\text{KOH}$ to yield isocyanide (foul smelling). This is the carbylamine test, which is not given by $2^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ amines.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a hypnotic drug?
questions.solution: Hypnotic drugs induce sleep and are habit forming; common examples are luminal and seconal.

questions.stem:
In the reaction

$\text{BF}_3 + 3\text{LiBH}_4 \rightarrow 3\text{LiF} + X$; $X$ is
questions.solution:
$$4\text{BF}_3 + 3\text{LiBH}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 + 3\text{LiBF}_4$$

The product $X$ is diborane, $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$.
questions.notes: printed equation in solution (2BF3 + 3LiBH4 -> 2B2H6 + 3LiF) is unbalanced; balanced form given

questions.stem: Which one of the following exhibits geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution: Alkenes having two different groups on each end of the double bond show geometrical isomerism ($\text{Ca}_2\text{b}_2$-type excluded; $\text{abC=Cab}$, $\text{abC=Ccd}$ types show it). 1,2-Dibromopropene and 2,3-dibromobut-2-ene qualify; 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene does not.

questions.stem: Magnesium burns in $\text{CO}_2$ to form
questions.solution: Mg burns in $\text{CO}_2$ to give MgO and C: $2\text{Mg} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + \text{C}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following catalyst is used in preparation of high density polythene?
questions.solution: High density polythene is formed when addition polymerisation of ethene takes place in a hydrocarbon solvent in presence of a catalyst such as Ziegler–Natta catalyst.

questions.stem: Which of the following acts as the stationary phase in paper chromatography?
questions.solution: Chromatography paper contains water trapped in it, which acts as the stationary phase.

questions.stem: Point out the false statement:

options.text: The colloidal solution of a liquid in liquid is called gel
Hardy Schulze rule is related with coagulation
Brownian movement and Tyndall effect are shown by colloidal system
Gold number is a measure of the protective power of lyophilic colloid

questions.solution: A colloid of liquid in liquid is called an emulsion. A colloid of liquid in solid is a gel.

questions.stem: Photochemical smog formed in congested metropolitan cities mainly consists of
questions.solution: Photochemical smog $\Rightarrow \text{O}_3$, PAN, $\text{NO}_x$.

questions.stem: In van der Waal's equation of state for a nonideal gas, the term that accounts for intermolecular forces is
questions.solution: $\left(P + \dfrac{a}{V^2}\right)(V - b) = RT$; here $\left(P + \dfrac{a}{V^2}\right)$ represents the intermolecular forces.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions of KCl will have the highest value of specific conductance?
questions.solution: The specific conductance increases with concentration, since the number of ions per $\text{cm}^3$ increases with increase of concentration.

questions.stem: Energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous constituent ions is called _____.
questions.solution: Lattice enthalpy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous constituent ions.

questions.stem: In a solid lattice, the cation has left a lattice site and is located at an interstitial position, the lattice defect is:
questions.solution: Frenkel defect is due to dislocation of an ion from its usual lattice site to an interstitial position.

questions.stem:
For the decomposition of azomethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{N}_2\text{CH}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3(g) + \text{N}_2(g)$ a first order reaction, the variation in partial pressure with time at $600$ K is given as shown in the figure.

The half life of the reaction is.
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction

$$k = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{P_0}{P} \Rightarrow \ln\frac{P}{P_0} = -kt$$

Comparing with $y = mx$: $k = -\text{slope} = 3.465 \times 10^{4}$

$$t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{3.465 \times 10^{4}} = 2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{s}$$
questions.notes: temperature partly cut off in image; 600 K assumed

questions.stem: If the radius of the 3rd Bohr's orbit of hydrogen atom is $r_3$ and the radius of 4th Bohr's orbit is $r_4$. Then:
questions.solution:
$r = 0.529 \times \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$ Å

$$r_3 = 0.529 \times \frac{3^2}{1},\quad r_4 = 0.529 \times \frac{4^2}{1} \Rightarrow \frac{r_4}{r_3} = \frac{16}{9} \Rightarrow r_4 = \frac{16r_3}{9}$$

questions.stem: How many elements are there in $6^{th}$ period of periodic table?
questions.solution: $6^{th}$ period consists of $32$ elements.

questions.stem: Observe the given boundary surface diagrams of two orbitals I and II and choose the correct option.
questions.solution: In boundary surface diagram I the four lobes lie between the $y$ and $z$ axes ($d_{yz}$), whereas in diagram II the four lobes lie on the $x$ and $y$ axes ($d_{x^2-y^2}$).

questions.stem:
Given that $E^\circ_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} = +1.23$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}/\text{SO}_4^{2-}} = 2.05$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-} = +1.09$ V; $E^\circ_{\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}} = +1.4$ V

The strongest oxidising agent is:
questions.solution: Reduction potential is maximum for $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$; therefore it is the strongest oxidising agent amongst the given species.

questions.stem: Given that bond energies of H $-$ H and Cl $-$ Cl are $430\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $240\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively and $\Delta H_f$ for HCl is $-90\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, bond enthalpy of HCl is
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{HCl}$

$\Delta H = \sum \text{B.E. of reactants} - \sum \text{B.E. of products}$

$$-90 = \frac{1}{2}\times 430 + \frac{1}{2}\times 240 - \text{B.E. of HCl}$$

$$\therefore \text{B.E. of HCl} = 215 + 120 + 90 = 425\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

questions.stem: The compounds $[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Br}_2$ and $[\text{PtBr}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl}_2$ constitutes a pair of
questions.solution: $[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Br}_2$ and $[\text{PtBr}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl}_2$ are ionisation isomers (the counter ion and ligand exchange places).

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules acts as a Lewis acid?
questions.solution: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{B}$ is electron deficient, thus behaves as a Lewis acid.

questions.stem: Thiamine and pyridoxine are also known respectively as:
questions.solution: Vitamin $\text{B}_1$ is also known as thiamine while vitamin $\text{B}_6$ is known as pyridoxine.

questions.stem:
Read the given passage carefully and select the best answer to each question out of the four given alternatives.

He was a vendor of sweets. He had his own peculiar method of advertising and doing business. He never depended upon others for help and worked hard all alone. I speak of Murali- the man who sold sweets. His customers were children, the future citizens of the world. At the stroke of nine in the morning, Murali would stand in front of the school with his tray of sweets. Till about eleven, the sale would be brisk. After that he moved off to other places. Even when the sweets became sticky in the heat, his business never slackened. There was depression in his business when the holidays came.

What time would he go to the school?
questions.solution: At the stroke of nine in the morning, Murali would stand in front of the school with his tray of sweets.

$$I = \int \frac{2a\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sqrt{a\sin^2\theta \cdot a\cos^2\theta}}\, d\theta = 2\int d\theta = 2\theta + c = 2\sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x/a}\right) + c$$

questions.stem: If $f(x) = \cos x$, $g(x) = \cos 2x$, $h(x) = \cos 3x$, and $I(x) = \tan x$, then which of the following options is correct?

options.text: $h(x)$ is neither increasing nor decreasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

questions.solution:
(a) $f'(x) = -\sin x < 0$ in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, so $f$ is strictly decreasing. $g'(x) = -2\sin 2x < 0$ in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ since $2x$ lies in the first or second quadrant, so $g$ is strictly decreasing.

(b) $h'(x) = -3\sin 3x$: in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$, $h'(x) < 0$; when $x \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $h'(x) > 0$ because $3x$ lies in the third quadrant. Hence $h$ is neither increasing nor decreasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

(c) $I'(x) = \sec^2 x > 0$ in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, so $I$ is strictly increasing.

All statements are correct.

$$\therefore \text{Modulus} = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2}$$

questions.solution:

questions.stem: The coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from the point $(2, 3)$ on the line $x + y - 11 = 0$ are
questions.solution:
Let $(h, k)$ be the foot. Slope of the perpendicular line is $\dfrac{k-3}{h-2}$; slope of the given line is $-1$.

$$\left(\frac{k-3}{h-2}\right)(-1) = -1 \Rightarrow k - h = 1 \quad \text{...(i)}$$

Since $(h, k)$ lies on the line: $h + k = 11$ ...(ii)

Solving, $h = 5$, $k = 6$. The foot is $(5, 6)$.

questions.stem: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & c & -b \\ -c & 0 & a \\ b & -a & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} a^2 & ab & ac \\ ab & b^2 & bc \\ ac & bc & c^2 \end{bmatrix}$, then $AB$ is equal to

questions.stem: If $y^x = e^{y - x}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Taking log: $x\log y = y - x$ ...(i)

Differentiating w.r.t. $x$:

$$\frac{x}{y}\frac{dy}{dx} + \log y = \frac{dy}{dx} - 1 \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{y} - 1\right) = -(1 + \log y)$$

From (i), $x = \dfrac{y}{1 + \log y}$:

$$\frac{dy}{dx}\left[\frac{1 - 1 - \log y}{1 + \log y}\right] = -(1 + \log y) \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{(1 + \log y)^2}{\log y}$$

Consider the function $f$ in $A = \mathbb{R} - \left\{\dfrac{2}{3}\right\}$ defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{4x + 3}{6x - 4}$, then $f^{-1}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:

$$6xy - 4y = 4x + 3 \Rightarrow x(6y - 4) = 3 + 4y \Rightarrow x = \frac{3 + 4y}{6y - 4}$$

questions.stem: The sum to infinite term of the series $1 + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{6}{3^2} + \dfrac{10}{3^3} + \dfrac{14}{3^4} + \cdots$ is
questions.solution:
$S = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{6}{3^2} + \dfrac{10}{3^3} + \cdots$ ...(i)

$\dfrac{1}{3}S = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3^2} + \dfrac{6}{3^3} + \cdots$ ...(ii)

Subtracting (ii) from (i):

$$\frac{2}{3}S = 1 + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{4}{3^2} + \frac{4}{3^3} + \cdots = \frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3^2} + \frac{4}{3^3} + \cdots = \frac{4/3}{1 - 1/3} = 2 \Rightarrow S = 3$$

questions.stem: The domain of the function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - \sqrt{1 - x^2}}$ is
questions.solution:
We need $x - \sqrt{1 - x^2} \ge 0$, i.e. $x \ge \sqrt{1 - x^2} \ge 0$, so $x \ge 0$ and $x^2 \ge 1 - x^2 \Rightarrow x^2 \ge \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x \le -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ or $x \ge \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Also $1 - x^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow -1 \le x \le 1$.

Thus $x \ge 0$, $x^2 \ge \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x^2 \le 1 \Rightarrow x \in \left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 1\right]$

If $(-4, 5)$ is one vertex and $7x - y + 8 = 0$ is one diagonal of a square, then the equation of second diagonal is
questions.solution:
Diagonals of a square are perpendicular and bisect each other. The vertex $(-4, 5)$ does not lie on $7x - y + 8 = 0$, so it lies on the other diagonal $y = mx + c$:

$5 = -4m + c$ ...(i)

The given diagonal has slope $7$, so $7m = -1 \Rightarrow m = -\dfrac{1}{7}$.

$$5 = \frac{4}{7} + c \Rightarrow c = \frac{31}{7}$$

$$y = -\frac{1}{7}x + \frac{31}{7} \Rightarrow x + 7y = 31$$

questions.stem: $\displaystyle\int \tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\, dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
By parts:

$$I = x\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \int \frac{1}{1+x}\cdot\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\cdot x\, dx = x\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \int\left(\frac{1+x}{(1+x)2\sqrt{x}} - \frac{1}{(1+x)2\sqrt{x}}\right)dx$$

$$= x\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \int\frac{dx}{2\sqrt{x}} + \int\frac{dx}{2\sqrt{x}(1+x)} = x\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + \tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} + C = (x+1)\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + C$$

questions.stem: The area of the region $R = \{(x, y) : 5x^2 \le y \le 2x^2 + 9\}$ is:
questions.solution:
The curves meet at $5x^2 = 2x^2 + 9 \Rightarrow x = \pm\sqrt{3}$, as shown in the figure.

$$\text{Area} = 2\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}(2x^2 + 9 - 5x^2)\,dx = 2[9x - x^3]_0^{\sqrt{3}} = 2[9\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}] = 12\sqrt{3}$$

questions.stem: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 - 1, & 0 < x < 2 \\ 2x + 3, & 2 \le x < 3 \end{cases}$, then the quadratic equation whose roots are $\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x)$ and $\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
$$\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}[(2 - h)^2 - 1] = \lim_{h \to 0}[h^2 - 4h + 3] = 3$$

$$\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}[2(2 + h) + 3] = 7$$

Quadratic with roots $3$ and $7$: $x^2 - (3 + 7)x + 3 \times 7 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0$

questions.stem: If the straight lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{k} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 3}{k} = \dfrac{z - 1}{2}$ intersect at a point, then the integer $k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
For intersecting lines the shortest distance is zero: $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1)\cdot(\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = 0$

$\vec{a}_1 = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}_1 = k\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{a}_2 = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b}_2 = 3\hat{i} + k\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

$$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & -2 \\ k & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & k & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 0 \Rightarrow 1(4 - 3k) - 1(2k - 9) - 2(k^2 - 6) = 0$$

$$\Rightarrow -2k^2 - 5k + 25 = 0 \Rightarrow k = -5 \text{ or } \frac{5}{2}$$

Integer $k = -5$.

questions.stem: If the co-ordinates of the point in which the line joining the points $(3, 5, -7)$ and $(-2, 1, 8)$ is intersected by the plane $yz$ is $\left[a, \dfrac{13}{b}, c\right]$, then $(a + b - c) =$

$\therefore a + b - c = 0 + 5 - 2 = 3$

questions.stem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $x = 3t^2 + 1$, $y = t^3 - 1$ at $x = 1$ is:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 6t$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3t^2$

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3t^2 \times \frac{1}{6t} = \frac{t}{2}$$

When $x = 1$: $1 = 3t^2 + 1 \Rightarrow t = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Hence, slope of the tangent $= 0$

questions.stem: A vector perpendicular to the plane containing the vectors $\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ is inclined to the vector $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ at an angle
questions.solution:
$$(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = -2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$$

Unit vector $\hat{a} = \dfrac{-2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}}{2\sqrt{5}}$

Angle with $\vec{r} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$:

$$\cos^{-1}\frac{\vec{r}\cdot\hat{a}}{|\vec{r}||\hat{a}|} = \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{15}} = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{14}$$

questions.stem: Minimum value of $Z = 3x + 5y$ subject to constraints $x + y \ge 2$, $x + 3y \ge 3$, $x, y \ge 0$
questions.solution:
Corner points of the (unbounded) feasible region: $(3, 0)$, $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, $(0, 2)$, giving $Z = 9, 7, 10$.

$Z$ is minimum $= 7$ at $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ (and $3x + 5y < 7$ has no common point with the region).

questions.stem: The roots of the given equation $(p - q)x^2 + (q - r)x + (r - p) = 0$ are:
questions.solution: $$x = \frac{(r - q) \pm \sqrt{(q - r)^2 - 4(r - p)(p - q)}}{2(p - q)} = \frac{(r - q) \pm (q + r - 2p)}{2(p - q)} = \frac{r - p}{p - q}, 1$$

questions.stem: How many different nine digit numbers can be formed from the number $223355888$ by rearranging its digits so that the odd digits occupy even positions
questions.solution:
There are $4$ odd digits $(3, 3, 5, 5)$ and $5$ even digits $(2, 2, 8, 8, 8)$, and $4$ even positions.

Ways to place odd digits in even places $= \dfrac{4!}{2!2!}$; ways to place even digits in odd places $= \dfrac{5!}{2!3!}$

Total $= \dfrac{4!}{2!2!} \times \dfrac{5!}{2!3!} = 6 \times 10 = 60$

questions.stem: The negation of the Boolean expression $((\sim q) \wedge p) \Rightarrow ((\sim p) \vee q)$ is logically equivalent to
questions.solution:
$\sim p \vee q \equiv p \rightarrow q$ and $\sim q \wedge p \equiv \sim(p \rightarrow q)$.

So the expression is $\sim(p \rightarrow q) \rightarrow (p \rightarrow q)$, whose negation is $\sim(p \rightarrow q) \wedge \sim(p \rightarrow q)$, i.e. $\sim(p \rightarrow q)$.

questions.stem: General solution of $\tan 5\theta = \cot 2\theta$ is (where $n \in I$):-
questions.solution:
$$\tan 5\theta = \cot 2\theta = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta\right) \Rightarrow 5\theta = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta$$

$$\Rightarrow 7\theta = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{n\pi}{7} + \frac{\pi}{14}$$
